newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc recovers further as tightness reappears.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc recovers further as tightness reappears.

text.p: LME zinc extended its recovery on Wednesday morning as tightness re-emerged, but the market was still smarting from a headlong plunge on Tuesday, traders said.
"The spread has done extremely well...I'm beginning to think that its not all over," said one trader.
The cash/threes spread flared to $100/$115 a tonne from around $70 at Tuesday's close, indicating residual tightness on nearby dates.
It showed up in the three month price, which breached $1,500 resistance in pre-market trade on Wednesday after crashing $300 to a low of $1,370 on Tuesday.
Prices hit $1,530, up $50 from Tuesday's kerb close and underpinned by moderate buying believed to originate in the Far East. The market was last indicated at $1,505/10.
Chinese officials said again some smelters remained short, but overall production capacity was enough to cover them.
But traders were nervous after Tuesday's violent correction that sliced 20 percent off Monday's seven-year high of $1,675.
"People are extremely nervous, they are very reluctant to sit on positions," a trader said.
Technical analysts expected choppy three month prices as they explore the current region to find a new range.
Other markets also took a look at the upside, with aluminium hitting a 19-month high.
Three month prices traded at $1,712, the highest since December 15, 1995 and up from the $1,700 afternoon kerb close on Tuesday.
Traders said a large U.S. investment bank was a big buyer on Tuesday and forward borrowing came early on Wednesday.
Borrowing was seen in threes/April while the threes/average 1998 flared to $37/$42 from $30 on Tuesday, traders said.
But forward selling by producers was capping the upside, they added.
Nickel broke through $7,500 and touched $7,560, a fresh two-month peak, before settling at $7,510/30.
This compared to Tuesday's close at $7,495.
Prices have gained nearly $750, or 11 percent, since last Friday, partly on the back of labour talks at Canada's Falconbridge on a contract that expires on Friday.

A news blackout was imposed on Tuesday ahead of the firm making an offer to workers. "The blackout should be taken as a positive sign that the negotiations have progressed and therefore we guess that the likelihood of a resolution has improved," broker GNI said in a commentary.
One dealer said the market may have a bit more upside in the short term, but it was approaching overbought levels.
Tin shook off its recent range, which had been capped at $5,460, after breaking above its 10-day moving average on Tuesday. It was last indicated at $5,515/35, compared to Tuesday's $5,410 close.
Lead was the laggard, dipping $5 to $630.
Alloy was indicated at $1,520/30, up $5/$10 from its previous close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
